answer: Proposed procurement voting: a proof for an onyx lot cannot cover willow timber or lantern oil lots. Each agent key must find SHA-256(beacon, lot, key, nonce) with at least 30 leading zero bits, using an unpredictable daily beacon. Validators check hashes and allow one vote per key/lot/day; missing or invalid proofs mean no vote. Hardware is reusable capital; energy is recurring expense, not stake. ASICs and cheap power lower costs. Key/lot/day binding prevents reuse: assuming ideal hashes, ten keys average 10 x 2^30 hashes per lot/day, even with shared hardware or parallel execution.
